scenes.title: Schema Change Detection & Enforcement
scenes.subtitle: Guarding structure against silent drift
scenes.narration: Schema monitoring detects when the structure of a dataset changes and enforces which changes are allowed to pass.

scenes.heading: Kinds of schema change
bullets: Data type changed, such as int to string
Column order changed in positional formats
scenes.narration: A dropped or renamed column can break every downstream query that references it. A changed data type can corrupt calculations or fail loads outright. Relaxed nullability lets nulls slip into fields that consumers assumed were always populated, and reordering matters in positional formats like CSV.

scenes.heading: Backward-compatible vs breaking
scenes.narration: Backward-compatible changes, like adding a nullable column, let existing consumers keep working without modification. Breaking changes, like dropping a column or narrowing a type, will fail or corrupt anything that depended on the old shape. Enforcement should permit the safe changes automatically and block the breaking ones until consumers are ready.

scenes.heading: Enforcing schema in code
scenes.narration: We declare the expected columns and their types as an explicit contract. The enforcement function compares the incoming frame against that contract, computing which columns are missing and which types drifted. If any breaking difference is found it raises immediately, stopping the bad batch before it can propagate.

scenes.text: Pin an expected schema, allow safe evolutions, and fail fast on breaking changes so consumers never break silently.
scenes.narration: Schema drift is one of the most common causes of broken dashboards. Treating the schema as an enforced contract turns a silent breakage into a clear, early failure.
